topics.title: Programming languages
topics.notes: Indices are zero-based throughout. Graph vertices are 0..n-1. Snippets are independent; adapt the entry point to the judge's input format. KACTL C++ algorithms use the rep/all/sz macros and ll/pii/vi aliases in the starter. Headers are independent recipes; do not concatenate the entire library.

snippets.title: C++ contest template
snippets.notes: The supplied template, including all helpers. print/println concatenate arguments: pass spaces explicitly. flintln flushes with endl; dbg writes to stdout, so remove debug calls before submission.

snippets.title: Java template
snippets.notes: Submit as Main.java. next() skips blank lines and returns null at EOF; nextInt() requires an available integer token. For a file, replace the reader with new FileReader("testfile.in"). Flush output after each interactive query.

snippets.title: Python template
snippets.notes: This example expects exactly three integers on one line. For larger input, use sys.stdin.buffer.readline; for interactive output, print(..., flush=True).

blocks.title: Complexity quick reference
blocks.notes: The source's input-size guide is a rough screening rule, not a runtime guarantee. Constants, language, hardware, memory and time limits matter. Estimate actual operation counts before choosing an algorithm.

facts.title: Common calls
facts.text: size(), empty(); begin()/end() delimit [first,last). Never dereference end(). front(), back(), top(), pop operations require nonempty containers. Most containers have clear(); stack, queue and priority_queue do not.

facts.title: Costs
facts.text: vector: index O(1), push_back amortized O(1), middle insert/erase O(n). deque: index/end operations O(1), middle edits O(n). stack/queue: O(1) on default storage. Heap: top O(1), push/pop O(log n).

facts.title: Ordered vs hashed
facts.text: set/map: lookup/insert/key erase O(log n); multiset allows duplicates; count/equal_range also depend on matches. unordered_set/map: expected O(1), worst O(n) per lookup/update; adversarial hashes can be slow. Use member lower_bound on trees; std::lower_bound can take O(n) iterator steps.

facts.title: Iterator lifetime
facts.text: vector reallocation invalidates all iterators/references; erase invalidates at/after the position. Tree insert preserves iterators, erase invalidates only erased elements. Hash rehash invalidates iterators. Avoid modifying a container while range-iterating unless validity is guaranteed.

snippets.title: C++ container API
snippets.notes: Independent call examples; replace values/types as needed. bitset<N> uses a compile-time N; bitwise operations process machine words. C++17 membership: find(x) != end() or count(x).

blocks.title: Arrays & collections
blocks.notes: Hash tables: expected O(1) lookup/insert/remove. Java hash iteration costs O(size+capacity). Python dict preserves insertion order; hash sets and Java HashMap have no guaranteed order. Array/list indexing is O(1); append is amortized O(1); middle insertion/removal and value search are O(n). Java generics use wrappers (Integer, not int).

snippets.title: Arrays, matrix, sort and search
snippets.notes: Arrays are fixed-size and zero-initialized (objects: null). Arrays.sort also accepts String[]. binarySearch requires the same ordering used to sort; an absent key returns -(insertion point)-1. Iterate each row's length for ragged matrices.

snippets.title: Lists and primitive arrays
snippets.notes: list is dynamic; array('i') stores C signed integers and can also append/pop. rows and cols must be nonnegative. Use independent row lists: [[0]*cols]*rows aliases rows.

snippets.title: ArrayList
snippets.notes: remove(int) removes by index; remove(Object) removes the first equal value. get/set/remove indices must exist; insertion allows index size().

snippets.title: Hash set
snippets.notes: Elements must be hashable. remove raises KeyError if absent; discard does not. pop removes an arbitrary element and raises KeyError on an empty set.

snippets.title: HashSet
snippets.notes: add/remove return whether the set changed. Duplicate insertion is ignored. Custom keys need consistent equals and hashCode.

snippets.title: Dictionary
snippets.notes: Keys must be hashable. d[key] raises KeyError if missing; get(key, fallback) is safe. Assignment and update overwrite existing values. Do not change dictionary size during iteration.

snippets.title: HashMap
snippets.notes: put/remove return the previous value, or null if absent. get can return null; unboxing null throws. containsValue is O(n). getOrDefault uses the fallback only for absent keys, not keys mapped to null.

snippets.title: Queue, stack and deque
snippets.notes: FIFO: offer/poll; LIFO: push/pop. ArrayDeque rejects null. peek/poll return null on empty; pop/removeFirst/removeLast throw. End insertions/removals are amortized O(1).

facts.title: Residues & overflow
facts.text: Use m > 0; normalize to [0,m). C++ % may be negative. Cast BEFORE arithmetic: (__int128)a*b; assigning a*b to __int128 afterwards is too late. Even (a%m+m)%m can overflow for large m. The helpers below accept signed 64-bit a,b and positive signed 64-bit m.

facts.title: Division & cancellation
facts.text: a/b mod m means a * inverse(b,m), defined only when gcd(b,m)=1. For example, inverse(3,8)=3 but inverse(2,8) does not exist. ax == ay mod m implies x == y mod (m/gcd(a,m)), not necessarily modulo m.
facts.latex: $a/b\pmod m$ means $a\,b^{-1}\pmod m$, defined only if $\gcd(b,m)=1$. Example: $3^{-1}\equiv3\pmod8$; $2^{-1}$ does not exist modulo 8. From $ax\equiv ay\pmod m$, infer $x\equiv y\pmod{m/\gcd(a,m)}$.

facts.title: Exponent rules
facts.text: Prime p: a^(p-1)=1 mod p only if p does not divide a; inverse(a,p)=a^(p-2) mod p. General m: a^phi(m)=1 mod m only if gcd(a,m)=1. Reduce exponents modulo p-1 or phi(m) only under these coprimality conditions. Negative exponents require an inverse.
facts.latex: Prime $p$: $a^{p-1}\equiv1\pmod p$ only if $p\nmid a$; then $a^{-1}\equiv a^{p-2}\pmod p$. General $m$: $a^{\phi(m)}\equiv1\pmod m$ only if $\gcd(a,m)=1$. Reduce exponents modulo $p-1$ or $\phi(m)$ only with these conditions. Negative exponents require an inverse.

facts.title: Linear congruences
facts.text: ax == b mod m: let g=gcd(a,m). Solvable iff g divides b; divide a,b,m by g and invert a/g modulo m/g. Exactly g residues modulo m: x0+k*(m/g), 0<=k<g. Example: 6x==8 mod14 gives x=6,13.
facts.latex: $ax\equiv b\pmod m$: let $g=\gcd(a,m)$. Solvable iff $g\mid b$; divide $a,b,m$ by $g$ and invert $a/g$ modulo $m/g$. Exactly $g$ residues: $x_0+k(m/g)$, $0\le k<g$. Example: $6x\equiv8\pmod{14}$ gives $x=6,13$.

facts.title: CRT compatibility
facts.text: x==a mod m and x==b mod n are compatible iff gcd(m,n) divides b-a. The merged solution is unique modulo lcm(m,n). Solve m*t==b-a mod n, then x=a+m*t. Use wide intermediates and ensure the combined modulus fits your type; see KACTL CRT below.
facts.latex: $x\equiv a\pmod m$, $x\equiv b\pmod n$ are compatible iff $\gcd(m,n)\mid(b-a)$. The solution is unique modulo $\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)$. Solve $mt\equiv b-a\pmod n$, then $x=a+mt$. Use wide intermediates and check that the combined modulus fits; see KACTL CRT below.

facts.title: Binomial coefficients
facts.text: For prime p and 0<=n<p, precompute fact[i]=i*fact[i-1] mod p, invfact[n]=fact[n]^(p-2) mod p, invfact[i-1]=i*invfact[i] mod p. Then C(n,k)=fact[n]*invfact[k]*invfact[n-k] mod p (0 if k outside [0,n]). O(n+log p) setup, O(1) query. For n>=p, factorial inversion fails; use Lucas/prime-power methods. For any modulus, Pascal recurrence works without division.
facts.latex: For prime $p$ and $0\le n<p$, precompute $f_i=i f_{i-1}\bmod p$, $h_n=f_n^{p-2}\bmod p$, $h_{i-1}=i h_i\bmod p$, with $f_0=1$. Then $\binom nk=f_nh_kh_{n-k}\bmod p$ (0 if $k\notin[0,n]$). $O(n+\log p)$ setup, $O(1)$ query. For $n\ge p$, factorial inversion fails; use Lucas/prime-power methods. Pascal recurrence works for any modulus without division.

facts.title: Geometric sums
facts.text: (1+r+...+r^(n-1))=(r^n-1)/(r-1) mod m only when r-1 is invertible. Without division, compute pair (r^n,S_n) by doubling: P_2n=P_n^2, S_2n=S_n*(1+P_n); append one term for odd n. Base P_0=1 mod m, S_0=0.
facts.latex: $S_n=1+r+\cdots+r^{n-1}=(r^n-1)/(r-1)\pmod m$ only if $r-1$ is invertible. Without division, double $(P_n,S_n)$: $P_{2n}=P_n^2$, $S_{2n}=S_n(1+P_n)$; append one term for odd $n$. Base $P_0=1\bmod m$, $S_0=0$.

snippets.title: Runtime modulus, inverse & congruence
snippets.notes: Requires the C++ template. inverse returns nullopt when no inverse exists (also for m=1); linear handles m=1 and a=0. All parameters are explicit; no hardcoded modulus. KACTL below adds discrete logs, modular roots, sieves and CRT.

blocks.title: Numeral systems
blocks.notes: For digits d[k]...d[0] in base b, value = sum(d[i]*b^i). Bases here are 2..36 with digits 0-9,a-z. Parsing invalid digits fails. Conversion takes O(number of digits) arithmetic steps; Python large-integer arithmetic has additional bit costs.

snippets.title: Parse and format any base
snippets.notes: Handles zero and negatives. bin adds 0b (negative values start -0b); format(x, 'b') omits the prefix. int(text, base) accepts upper/lower-case letters.

snippets.title: Integer base conversions
snippets.notes: parseInt requires a signed 32-bit result, otherwise NumberFormatException. toBinaryString prints negative ints as 32-bit two's complement; toString(value, 2) prints a minus sign. Use .equals for Java string comparisons.

blocks.title: Graphs & grids
blocks.notes: Adjacency lists use O(V+E) space. Add u->v for directed edges; add both directions for an undirected edge. DFS/BFS visit reachable vertices in O(V+E) time, O(V) extra space. An outer loop covers disconnected graphs; its roots count components only for undirected graphs. Mark on insertion to avoid duplicate stack/queue entries.

snippets.title: DFS: reachability and forest
snippets.notes: Build adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]. Explicit stack avoids recursion depth limits. Traversal order may differ from recursive DFS; this version is for reachability, not recursive entry/exit times.

snippets.title: DFS: adjacency list and forest
snippets.notes: graph(n) allocates n independent lists. Iterative reachability traversal; use an explicit call-frame stack when recursive entry/exit order matters.

snippets.title: BFS: distances and forest
snippets.notes: dist[v] is the shortest number of edges from start; -1 means unreachable. Requires an unweighted graph. bfs_forest covers all vertices, without assigning unrelated roots a common distance.

snippets.title: BFS: distances and forest
snippets.notes: The source examples used a queue; ArrayDeque gives amortized O(1) end operations. Mark each vertex before enqueueing it.

snippets.title: Four-neighbor flood fill
snippets.notes: Rectangular grid. fill counts the unseen cells of the starting color reachable from (r,c), and updates seen. components returns all same-color region sizes. O(rows*cols) time and space overall; empty grids are supported.

facts.title: Cost & lifetime
facts.text: Index/size: O(1); substr copies O(count); middle insert/erase/replace: O(n); find can be O(n*m) for pattern length m. Appending a character is amortized O(1). string_view is a non-owning view: the source must outlive it and not invalidate its storage. Byte indexing is not Unicode character indexing.

snippets.title: String calls, parsing & input
snippets.notes: substr(pos,count) truncates count at the end but throws if pos > size(). npos is unsigned: compare with string::npos; never test p >= 0. cctype functions require unsigned char conversion (or EOF).

facts.title: Comparator contract
facts.text: comp(a,b) means a precedes b; it must be a strict weak ordering. Use <, never <=; comp(x,x) must be false. For tie breakers use tie(a.first,a.second) < tie(b.first,b.second), not subtraction (overflow). sort is unstable; stable_sort preserves equivalent elements.

facts.title: Captures
facts.text: [] none; [x] snapshot by value; [&x] by reference; [=] implicit copies; [&] implicit references; [x,&y] mixed. mutable allows changing captured copies. Reference captures must outlive the lambda; a copied pointer still refers to the original object. Use -> ReturnType for explicit/recursive return types.

facts.title: Useful algorithms
facts.text: sort and nth_element need random-access iterators. unique removes adjacent duplicates logically and returns a new end: erase the tail. next_permutation returns false and resets to ascending at the final permutation. min_element/max_element return end() for empty ranges; accumulate(...,0LL) uses a 64-bit sum.

snippets.title: Sorting, bounds & lambda syntax
snippets.notes: All iterator ranges are half-open. stable_sort is O(n log n) with enough extra memory, otherwise up to O(n log^2 n) comparisons. Lambda recursion shown below requires passing itself explicitly: fib(fib,n).

snippets.title: Binary search / first true
snippets.notes: binary_search requires an ascending sorted sequence; it returns any matching index or -1. first_true requires a false-then-true predicate on integer indices in [lo, hi). Example lower bound: first_true(0, len(a), lambda i: a[i] >= x). O(log n) predicate calls, O(1) auxiliary space.

snippets.title: Kadane: maximum subarray sum
snippets.notes: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space. Handles all-negative input; a must be nonempty. ending is the best sum ending at the current position.

snippets.title: Parity, masks, XOR and shifts
snippets.notes: XOR identities: x^x=0, x^0=x. unique assumes all other values occur an even number of times. XOR swap uses distinct storage; a temporary variable is clearer. x<<k multiplies by 2^k only without overflow; signed x>>k rounds toward negative infinity, unlike Java integer division for negative values. >>> shifts in zero bits. int shifts mask k with 31; long shifts mask with 63. Use 1L<<bit for long masks. Bit operations are not automatically faster than equivalent arithmetic.
